summary: WebSocket-driven PTY grants remote shell and filesystem control on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs an agent that opens a WebSocket connection to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL) and dispatches incoming JSON messages to handlers that spawn a PTY (bash/pwsh/cmd via @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch) and forward server-supplied bytes directly into it. In connection/index.js the socket 'message' handler routes to message-router.js, whose 'terminal_input' case calls term.pty.write(msg.data) in terminal.js, giving whoever controls the WebSocket endpoint interactive shell execution on the host running the agent. Additional message types expose arbitrary file read/write/delete/move/copy, git operations, file upload/download, and an HTTP/WS proxy. On startup (unless YEAFT_SKIP_STARTUP_INSTALLS=true), index.js also git-clones https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev, git pull --ff-only on subsequent runs, chmod 0755 hook scripts, and enables the plugin in ~/.claude/settings.json — an unpinned HEAD pull of a publisher-matched repo whose hook scripts execute inside the Claude plugin sandbox. service/linux.js modifies PATH to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin as part of the service installer.
